title: Mice, a Caved-In Ceiling, and Cloudy Water: The GSA’s New Office Is Falling Apart
gist: About 1,600 GSA and OPM employees relocated to a dilapidated federal building after DOGE-driven workforce cuts and a federal real-estate disposition push at GSA, illustrating the physical and organizational fallout of the Trump administration's government-efficiency agenda.

insights.claim: GSA, the federal agency responsible for government IT services and real estate, was hit early by DOGE cuts starting January 2025, effectively firing tens of thousands of workers and imposing return-to-office and zero-based budgeting requirements, but a year later GSA announced plans to hire about 400 workers.
insights.speaker: Zoë Schiffer
insights.so_what: A cut-then-rehire cycle at a major federal operations agency signals DOGE-style austerity is proving partially unsustainable, relevant to tracking federal workforce/contracting demand normalization.
insights.locator: The federal workforce has been rocked by changes

insights.claim: As part of a 'government-wide effort to reduce underutilized space and fortify the federal real estate footprint,' GSA is pursuing 'accelerated disposition,' or quick sale, of hundreds of federal office buildings, including the building housing the relocated GSA/OPM staff, which is slated for sale despite housing employees until December 2028.
insights.speaker: Zoë Schiffer
insights.so_what: A multi-year wave of federal office building disposals is a supply event for commercial real estate and could create opportunities for buyers/redevelopers, but also shows a long tail (2028) before disposition completes.
insights.quote: government-wide effort to reduce underutilized space and fortify the federal real estate footprint
insights.locator: GSA leadership, including administrator Ed Forst

insights.claim: About 1,600 federal employees from GSA and the Office of Personnel Management were forced to relocate to the Theodore Roosevelt Federal Building, which workers describe as having mice, a caved-in bathroom ceiling, and drinking water requiring a 5-10 second flush before it runs clear, while their original F Street building undergoes renovation.
insights.speaker: Zoë Schiffer
insights.so_what: A visible degradation in federal facility conditions during an active real-estate divestiture is a proxy indicator of deferred maintenance and reduced capital spending on government-owned property during the cost-cutting period.
insights.quote: We’re left wondering what else is going to collapse or break—do we need to look at the ceiling before going to the bathroom?

insights.claim: While Elon Musk has stepped back from his public DOGE role, DOGE affiliates continue working inside government pushing austerity and AI initiatives, while others have exited to the private sector to work in AI, data centers, and manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Zoë Schiffer
insights.so_what: A talent pipeline from DOGE-era government cost-cutting roles into AI/data-center/manufacturing private-sector jobs is a small but notable labor-flow signal for those sectors.
